name: Autechre
hook: Two friends from Rochdale who started by cutting up hip-hop and electro on a cassette deck and became Warp's furthest-out act.
blurb: Rob Brown and Sean Booth grew up near Manchester in the 1980s, listening to electro, hip-hop and acid house. They made cassette mixes together, pausing and restarting the tape to cut records into new shapes, copying producers like Mantronix, whose edit-heavy production Booth has named as a major influence. That start in hip-hop editing, well documented in their own interviews, makes them a quiet link between lineages on this map. The 1987 start year is an estimate of when the pair began working together. In 1992 Warp put two of their tracks on Artificial Intelligence, and their first album, Incunabula, came out on Warp in 1993. Their later records grow steadily more abstract, and more built on computer-generated rules.
